history_of_present_illness: The patient presented with a 3-year history of left-sided scrotal swelling that was non-tender and gradually increased in size, without fever, and previous attempts at traditional herbal medicine were unsuccessful.
exposure_and_epidemiology: The patient is from the central part of Myanmar, a region where scrotal swelling is reported to be common.
physical_exam: Fair general condition with unilateral, non-tender, non-reducible scrotal swelling and no palpable inguinal lymph nodes.
labs_and_diagnostics: Ultrasound was performed, which confirmed hydrocoele and can help distinguish testicular tumors or hernias, and may show adult worms (filarial dance sign) in lymphatic filariasis.
differential_diagnosis: Inguinal hernia, hydrocoele, testicular tumor, lymphatic filariasis (caused by Wuchereria bancrofti), urogenital schistosomiasis (not endemic in Southeast Asia), and testicular tuberculosis.
management_and_clinical_course: The patient underwent hydrocoelectomy, where 3 litres of clear fluid were drained, and received antifilarial treatment. He was subsequently lost to follow-up.
final_diagnosis: Hydrocoele, confirmed by ultrasound, with lymphatic filariasis as the likely underlying cause.
